Tincuta Heinzel is a designer and researcher with a background in visual arts, design, and cultural anthropology. She completed her PhD in 2012 at Paris 1 University Panthéon-Sorbonne (France) with a thesis on electronic and reactive textiles' aesthetics. She initiated, curated, and or coordinated several projects, such as “Artists in Industry” (Bucharest, 2011–2013) and “Haptosonics” (Oslo, 2013). Under what she labels as “aesthetics of imperceptibility,” Tincuta investigates the aesthetic issues of nano-materiality and design's new roles as operator between scales. V. V. Vadher was born in Kenya in 1950. After moving to England in 1967, he served an apprenticeship with Herbert Morris (U.K.) Ltd from 1968 to 1973, obtaining a B.Sc degree with First-class Honours and an IEE Prize from the University of Aston in 1973. During 1973-74 he was a design and development engineer on electronidelectrical control systems for cranes with Herbert Morris. In 1975 he moved to Linear Motors Ltd, and in 1977 he was awarded an M.Phil. and a DIC by Imperial College, London, for his work on linear induction motors. Also in 1977 he became a research worker at Loughborough University of Technology, gaining the degree of Ph.D. in 1981 for work on the mathematical modelling of the type of power supply system found onboard ships, aircraft, etc. He is presently a lecturer in the Department of Electronic and Electrical Engineering at Loughborough, where his research interests are in the design and mathematical modelling of power supply systems, linear induction motors, special-purpose electrical machines and networks, and travelling waveinduction heaters
